Digital Human Video

Use one shared presenter workflow and route-specific video methods. This package contains all routing, identity, and execution instructions; do not invoke another Skill, open Casting Room, or create an MCP App to complete a route.

Route the user's query

Infer the desired result from the current query, supplied material, and prior approved work. Choose by the viewer's job, not by a matching platform or topic word. Read only the selected route reference, plus shared references when needed.

RouteUser's intended resultExample queryRead
assetCreate/save a reusable presenter or fill an existing Element's Look/voice gaps"Create a digital human first, add an office look, and do not make a video"Asset method [blocked]
socialA short direct-to-camera message, announcement, or general social explanation"Have the digital human deliver this script as a Reels talking-head video"Social method [blocked]
propertyHelp viewers evaluate or visit a specific real property, venue, or facility with guide-to-space cutaways"Make a TikTok video introducing this hotel"Property method [blocked]
productDemonstrate/promote a product's value, feature, or use with presenter-to-product cutaways and product evidence"Have a digital human demo this app's new feature and end with a trial call to action"Product method [blocked]
courseTeach a skill or process with an observable learning outcome, alternating on-camera presenter delivery and teaching visuals"Teach new users how to export a report in this app"Course method [blocked]
marketExplain dated developments, trends, or changes using sources and data"Report this week's property-market changes"Market method [blocked]
newsReport current events or a news story from network-searched sources with source-labelled visual evidence"Report today's AI industry news"News method [blocked]

Apply these precedence rules:

  1. A local revision stays with its existing route. "Only change the CTA" or "Replace the second shot" reuses the existing brief, presenter, and accepted assets. Ask for the target artifact only if it cannot be identified; do not restart onboarding.

  2. Explicit outcomes outrank channel and subject. A TikTok hotel tour is property; a property-market update is market; a current-event bulletin is news; a software lesson is course; a persuasive software launch demo is product. General short speech is social when a more specific outcome does not apply.

  3. Missing identity is a prerequisite, not a route change. "There is no person yet; make a product demo" remains product with the shared production sequence below. Create or reuse its character subject without adding an unrequested actor package, multiple Looks, or voice library.

  4. Combine only requested deliverables. If the user requests a tour and a market update, plan two deliverables under property and market, reuse the adopted presenter, and keep each script, evidence ledger, and output state separate. If they request a reusable presenter plus a video, use the shared sequence once; saving the subject also fulfills the asset deliverable.

  5. Ask one outcome question only when needed. For an ambiguous "product walkthrough", use the CTA, audience, and supplied script to distinguish promotion from instruction. If still unresolved, ask whether viewers should choose the product or learn to complete a task. Do not make users select internal route names or six modules.

  6. Object and space outcomes require cutaways. A product or property brief that contains a physical product, software interface, room, venue, building, or amenity must include a shot plan with presenter A-roll and subject cutaways. Do not deliver an all-presenter talking head when the viewer needs to inspect the thing being introduced. social and market stay presenter-led unless their brief explicitly requests supporting inserts.

  7. Course outcomes require teaching visuals. A course brief must map each learning beat to on-camera presenter A-roll, GPT-generated explanatory B-roll, deterministic HTML/CSS/JS recording, supplied capture, or uploaded B-roll. When a visual carries the concept, alternate A-roll and B-roll in the shot plan and read Course method [blocked]; do not deliver an all-presenter lesson or an unordered asset list.

  8. News outcomes require network research and recorded evidence. A news brief must search the network before scripting, preserve a source ledger and cut-off time, and render source-labelled HTML evidence as B-roll. Every HTML-to-video path must use the installed ffmpeg and headless Chromium chain; read News method [blocked] and do not present search snippets, stale pages, or an all-presenter bulletin as the finished news deliverable.

The route is internal planning state. Explain the intended deliverable in the user's language. If the request falls outside these outcomes, explain the scope instead of forcing it into a digital-human workflow.

Shared presenter gate

Inspect explicit attachments and selected Canvas/Element references. Reuse an authorized single-person identity that the user has chosen; never select the latest node, a filename, or a person from a group photo by inference. The identity gate is the visual anchor only; it does not approve the keyframe previs, voice, character subject, or video.

For a local revision, reuse the identity recorded in the existing project. A text or overlay-only edit that creates no new presenter media does not reopen this gate.

If no person is supplied, read Presenter identity [blocked]: one ordinary show_form, exact account-available Midjourney v8.2, a 2:3 headshot on #808080, a short English prompt ending in --style raw, exact-result inspection, then explicit user adoption. Do not require a provider output count or reject a supported Midjourney result because of its returned shape. Use the route's live structured parameters for ratio, resolution, and quality. Do not use a beauty fallback or nearby-version fallback.

Keep the selected business route while waiting. Before identity adoption, do not generate presenter media. Already supplied facts and copy remain inputs; never discard or recollect them. Once adopted, the same exact face reference serves every route.

Required production sequence

For a new presenter-led video, keep this order. Skip a stage only when its approved artifact already exists and is still valid for the requested change.

  1. Lock the brief and aspect. Collect audience, objective, script or topic, duration, and orientation. Use landscape 16:9 or portrait 9:16 according to the brief; if it is genuinely ambiguous, ask before generating. Resolve the live model contract for the exact ratio instead of guessing a provider parameter.

  2. Create the visual identity. Reuse an explicitly approved person or follow Presenter identity [blocked] to use Midjourney v8.2 for the raw headshot. The prompt must describe one person and one casting headshot; do not turn it into multiple casting options or enumerate candidate identities. Inspect the result(s) returned by the live route and wait for explicit adoption of one face anchor; keep that anchor fixed afterward.

  3. Select and fix the voice. Reuse an approved voice. For a user-designated upload, inspect its exact audio reference and bind it as voice_ref; an explicit request to use that voice counts as selection. Do not generate alternative voices for it. Otherwise resolve the newest available Seed Audio model, generate a small voice candidate set (default two) using the same short audition line, let the user listen and choose, and bind that result as voice_ref. Use fast, clear speech and lively intonation. Read the live model contract before generating; do not hard-code an assumed latest version. Keep this voice identity for every subsequent audio job.

  4. Build and confirm the keyframe scene. After the face and voice are approved, use the live GPT 2.5 model contract to make the minimum keyframe previs for the requested scene(s), with the selected person, scene, action, framing, and locked 16:9 or 9:16 ratio. Pass the adopted face as the identity reference; describe a real human in a live-action scene. For product and property, include the subject in the keyframe plan: presenter framing, presenter_with_object or presenter_in_space when the relation matters, product/space hero, close-up or detail, and the return to the presenter. Generate one keyframe per distinct composition. For course, cover the presenter, concept_visual, worked_example, and any screen_demo or html_recording frame required by the learning beat. For news, cover the news_anchor, headline/source card, timeline, chart/map/quote frame, and return to the anchor needed by the source claims. A continuous shot can reuse its approved keyframe across several audio segments. Use a few concise sentences for person, action, framing, setting, object/space detail, and light. Put aspect, count, and quality in supported structured parameters. Inspect the exact person-in-scene and subject keyframes and get explicit approval.

  5. Create the character subject. Only after the keyframe scene is approved, create or update the character subject/Element through the current persistence contract. Bind the adopted face, selected voice_ref, approved scene/keyframe references, and only the requested Look assets. Preserve unrelated members.

  6. Generate the first talking scene. Prepare the first scene's spoken audio with the selected Seed Audio voice anchor with fast delivery and lively, varied intonation, then use Seedance 2.5 for the first talking-video segment and the continuation workflow. Seedance 2.0 or MiniMax H3 remain alternatives for separate video requests when selected by the user; never silently switch an explicitly chosen model. The video prompt must require a real human presenter, fast but clear speech, varied expressions that follow the meaning, natural eye contact, head movements, and gestures. Bind the character subject, approved keyframe, scene-one audio, exact spoken copy, locked aspect, and timing. For product and property, generate presenter and cutaway source clips as separate shot units, then assemble their approved order on the timeline. For course, generate presenter A-roll and each teaching B-roll unit separately; record approved HTML/CSS/JS visuals before assembly and export the assembled lesson timeline to Canvas through the supported path. Inspect the exact completed first scene and its first teaching or subject cutaway before continuing. For news, search and verify the source ledger before writing the final lines, then generate the presenter A-roll and source-labelled HTML B-roll separately. Any HTML-to-video recording must use the installed ffmpeg and headless Chromium chain before the assembled bulletin is exported to Canvas.

    Reuse this compact performance clause in each video prompt, then add only the scene-specific action and continuity details:

    text
    A real person on camera, with a natural live-action look; a fast pace with clear articulation, varied intonation, expressions that follow the meaning, natural coordination of the eyes, head, and gestures, a relaxed body, and fluid movement.

  7. Make the next scene audio and extend. After the first scene is accepted, generate the next scene's audio with the same voice_ref and the current Seed Audio contract. Extend the continuous presenter A-roll in Seedance 2.5 using the immediately preceding accepted presenter video, the new scene audio, the same subject, and supported scene/keyframe context. For product and property, put approved B-roll over the A-roll in the final timeline. For course, place each approved teaching visual under the matching voice_span; HTML recordings and source captures remain independent B-roll unless the live contract explicitly supports their continuation. Only use a direct A→B or B→A video continuation when the live contract explicitly supports that shot-type change; otherwise generate the B-roll independently and keep its voiceover span in the renderer manifest. Scene 2 uses scene 1's accepted predecessor, scene 3 uses scene 2's accepted predecessor, and so on. Keep voice, aspect, and performance consistent. Follow the runtime contract for continuity, output overlap, and audio timing; stop when the complete approved script has been spoken and the requested deliverable is covered. For news, keep the source-labelled HTML B-roll independent unless the live contract explicitly supports a shot-type change, and assemble it under the matching verified news voice_span.

Product and property cutaway layer

Read the selected Product method [blocked] or Property method [blocked] for the route-specific shot grammar. The shared rule is:

  • Keep presenter speech, product/space visuals, and sourced proof as separate shot units. A cutaway may carry the continuing approved voiceover, but it must not be hidden inside a talking-head generation prompt.
  • Give every shot a shot_type, source_ref, script_span, voice_span, duration, transition point, and acceptance state. Use presenter for A-roll, presenter_with_object or presenter_in_space for a person-subject relationship, object_hero or object_detail for product views, demo_action for use, and space_wide, space_detail, or amenity for property views.
  • Alternate on purpose: presenter establishes the claim, the product or space proves it visually, and the presenter returns for interpretation or CTA. Do not cut on every sentence or use an insert that has no spoken or evidentiary role.
  • Generate object/space clips separately from presenter clips. For a real product, UI, address, room, amenity, measurement, label, or price, use supplied or captured source media whenever exact appearance matters. Generated subject footage is illustrative until matched to an approved source. Keep pure B-roll prompts short: object/space, shot size, action, light, and continuity detail. Use the real-human, fast, expressive performance clause only for presenter or presenter_with_object shots, never for a product/space-only closeup.
  • Assemble only after the individual clips and their audio spans are approved. Check that cuts preserve the fixed person, product identity, spatial orientation, speech continuity, safe areas, and readable labels. An ordered clip list is partial when a rendered master was requested.

Course teaching B-roll layer

Read the selected Course method [blocked] for the full teaching contract. The shared rule is:

  • Keep on-camera presenter A-roll and teaching B-roll as separate shot units. Use presenter for goals, explanations, judgment, correction, recap, and practice; use presenter_with_visual when the relationship between the person and visual is itself instructional.
  • Use concept_visual for an illustrative GPT visual, html_recording for exact UI/code/formula/chart/table/timeline states, screen_demo for supplied or captured procedures, worked_example for sourced calculations, and caption_card for exact definitions or warnings. Do not use generated imagery as an exact UI, live-data, official-chart, or completed-experiment substitute.
  • Give every teaching unit a learning_step or claim_id, visual_mode, source_ref or html_artifact_ref, script_span, voice_span, duration, cut-in/cut-out, evidence_role, and review_state. For HTML, also record the artifact version, viewport, frame rate, duration, start/end state, and recording reference before export.
  • Keep approved voiceover under silent B-roll only within its matching voice_span; return to on-camera presenter delivery for interpretation, correction, emphasis, recap, or the next action. Cut on a teaching event such as a visual reveal, code action, formula change, or worked result instead of cutting only for variety.
  • Export the assembled course timeline to Canvas through the supported renderer or write-back path and read back the returned Canvas reference. An HTML preview, local recording, A-roll clip set, or unordered B-roll list is partial when a lesson video was requested.

News bulletin layer

Read the selected News method [blocked] before planning a news video. News is a source-verification and visual-evidence route, not a generic market or talking-head route:

  • Search the network before writing the final script or generating news visuals. Fix the source cutoff time, timezone, geography, language, audience, and freshness window. Prefer primary sources, then independently corroborate material claims. Keep facts, source claims, interpretation, and unresolved items separate.
  • Give every claim a source URL/document, title, publication or update time, search and access time, source type, status, exact source span, and claim_id. A 403, login wall, missing date, or stale page is an access/freshness gap, not proof that no update exists.
  • Use a deliberate A/B sequence: news_anchor says what happened, source-labelled HTML B-roll shows the headline, timeline, chart, map, quote, or source strip, and the anchor returns to explain impact, uncertainty, or the next item. Keep each B-roll unit tied to one verified claim_id and voice_span.
  • Any HTML-to-video or page-recording path is fixed to the installed stack: ffmpeg and headless Chromium are installed. Headless Chromium renders the deterministic page at the locked viewport; ffmpeg encodes or packages the captured frames and audio into video. A browser preview, HTML file, or search-result screenshot is not a finished video. Record browser/ffmpeg versions, viewport, fps, duration, start/end state, output reference, source cutoff, and Canvas reference.
  • Export the assembled bulletin to Canvas and read back the returned reference. If network search, source ledger, fixed-stack recording, or Canvas write-back is unavailable, report the news result as partial and preserve the exact gap.

Do not add a separate image or exploratory keyframe generation stage solely to create selection candidates, and do not force a provider-specific image count. Keep the Midjourney prompt focused on one person; use the result shape returned by the live route and bind only the image the user explicitly adopts as the face anchor. Voice candidates remain the intentional selection set. If a visual, voice, or video result is rejected, regenerate only that stage after the user supplies a changed direction; keep approved stages and references unchanged.

Use "real human" and positive performance direction in generation prompts. Do not label the subject “digital human”, “AI avatar”, or “virtual presenter”, even in a stock negative clause. Avoid stiff posture, frozen expressions, mechanical nodding, or looping gestures in the result. This describes the desired visual performance; retain truthful synthetic-media context in delivery.

Shared execution

  1. Establish the brief. Read the selected route's method, reuse known inputs, and collect only blocking gaps: audience, objective, exact facts/source media, script or prompt, orientation, duration, voice, and final deliverables.
  2. Plan the staged artifacts. Preserve supplied exact copy. For a topic prompt, produce the full spoken script, compact GPT 2.5 presenter/subject keyframe prompts, shot plan, cutaway and teaching-visual source list, per-claim source ledger, and per-scene audio lines before generation. For course, choose a visual mode for every beat (gpt_visual, html_recording, source_capture, or uploaded_broll) before generation. For news, complete network search and the source ledger before final script, HTML, or A-roll generation. Reuse existing approval for unchanged work. Asset-only requests follow asset.md and do not enter video production.
  3. Record dependencies. Track route, aspect, identity reference/state, keyframe references, approved script, voice candidates and selected voice_ref, character subject, facts/sources, scene ids, shot types, cutaway source refs, spoken lines/audio results, media/reference roles, overlay/caption text, teaching learning_step/claim_id, visual mode, HTML artifact and recording references, news source URL/title/published-at/accessed-at/status/cutoff fields, browser and ffmpeg versions, viewport, fps, timing, cut order, segment chain, exact job/result references, Canvas export and read-back references, review state, and export state. This is a project manifest, not a new Element schema or backend API.
  4. Execute the current contract. Read Runtime contract [blocked] before generation, media inspection, persistence, or rendering. Use standard TapNow CLI and existing forms. For every HTML-to-video/page-recording task, verify the installed stack exactly as ffmpeg and headless Chromium are installed before capture; do not substitute a browser preview or an untracked recorder. A source reference, submitted job, completed media result, inspected result, and final export are distinct states.
  5. Review the smallest changed unit. Keep the face anchor, keyframes, voice, and accepted assets fixed. Re-render changed information cards without regenerating the presenter; regenerate a spoken line only when speech changed. Changing a scene's audio regenerates that scene's video. A changed video invalidates downstream continuations that used it as their source; preserve earlier scenes and recheck or regenerate affected continuations. A new identity invalidates dependent presenter visuals; a new voice invalidates dependent speech and talking video. For product or property work, a changed object/space source invalidates only the affected cutaway and any downstream assembly that depends on its timing. For course, a changed claim, formula, code result, HTML artifact, source capture, or learning step invalidates its teaching shot, narration/caption timing, and dependent assembly, while preserving unrelated chapters. For news, a changed source, cutoff, claim, date, number, quote, or HTML evidence card invalidates that claim's source ledger row, A-roll line, B-roll recording, captions, and dependent assembly.
  6. Deliver the real result. Match the requested asset or video scope. A full business video requires an actual assembled export; an A-roll clip or ordered segment set is partial when assembly was requested. Report missing runtime capabilities and remaining work precisely. Do not publish externally.

Interaction and acceptance

  • Keep form submission, identity adoption, voice confirmation, keyframe-previs approval, subject creation, platform cost confirmation, and final review separate. Honor authorization already given for the same scope; do not stack duplicate forms or add confirmation at every scene.
  • Preserve the presenter's truthful role. Generated presenters do not create evidence of customer experience, credentials, real locations, product performance, or financial outcomes. Apply the selected route's specific evidence rules.
  • Inspect exact completed media for identity continuity, fixed voice, complete speech, lip sync, fast clear delivery, expressive natural movement, facts, caption/chart legibility, teaching order, HTML/screen readability, timing, cut order, cutaway continuity, product/space identity, news source ledger and cutoff, publication/ access times, fixed ffmpeg + headless Chromium recording state, Canvas export state, safe areas, and the CTA or next learning action. Frozen faces, stiff movement, repeated gestures, voice drift, unexplained cuts, or skipped/repeated lines fail review. State which checks could not run; structural validation alone is not visual acceptance.
  • Deliver exact asset/media references, the script or captions when relevant, sources/rights and synthetic-presenter context, unresolved items, and the actual export status. Do not promise virality, sales, or guaranteed outcomes.

Digital Human Video

Use one shared presenter workflow and route-specific video methods. This package contains all routing, identity, and execution instructions; do not invoke another Skill, open Casting Room, or create an MCP App to complete a route.

Route the user's query

Infer the desired result from the current query, supplied material, and prior approved work. Choose by the viewer's job, not by a matching platform or topic word. Read only the selected route reference, plus shared references when needed.

Apply these precedence rules:

A local revision stays with its existing route. "Only change the CTA" or "Replace the second shot" reuses the existing brief, presenter, and accepted assets. Ask for the target artifact only if it cannot be identified; do not restart onboarding.

Explicit outcomes outrank channel and subject. A TikTok hotel tour is property; a property-market update is market; a current-event bulletin is news; a software lesson is course; a persuasive software launch demo is product. General short speech is social when a more specific outcome does not apply.

Missing identity is a prerequisite, not a route change. "There is no person yet; make a product demo" remains product with the shared production sequence below. Create or reuse its character subject without adding an unrequested actor package, multiple Looks, or voice library.

Combine only requested deliverables. If the user requests a tour and a market update, plan two deliverables under property and market, reuse the adopted presenter, and keep each script, evidence ledger, and output state separate. If they request a reusable presenter plus a video, use the shared sequence once; saving the subject also fulfills the asset deliverable.

Ask one outcome question only when needed. For an ambiguous "product walkthrough", use the CTA, audience, and supplied script to distinguish promotion from instruction. If still unresolved, ask whether viewers should choose the product or learn to complete a task. Do not make users select internal route names or six modules.

Object and space outcomes require cutaways. A product or property brief that contains a physical product, software interface, room, venue, building, or amenity must include a shot plan with presenter A-roll and subject cutaways. Do not deliver an all-presenter talking head when the viewer needs to inspect the thing being introduced. social and market stay presenter-led unless their brief explicitly requests supporting inserts.

Course outcomes require teaching visuals. A course brief must map each learning beat to on-camera presenter A-roll, GPT-generated explanatory B-roll, deterministic HTML/CSS/JS recording, supplied capture, or uploaded B-roll. When a visual carries the concept, alternate A-roll and B-roll in the shot plan and read Course method [blocked]; do not deliver an all-presenter lesson or an unordered asset list.

News outcomes require network research and recorded evidence. A news brief must search the network before scripting, preserve a source ledger and cut-off time, and render source-labelled HTML evidence as B-roll. Every HTML-to-video path must use the installed ffmpeg and headless Chromium chain; read News method [blocked] and do not present search snippets, stale pages, or an all-presenter bulletin as the finished news deliverable.

The route is internal planning state. Explain the intended deliverable in the user's language. If the request falls outside these outcomes, explain the scope instead of forcing it into a digital-human workflow.

Shared presenter gate

Inspect explicit attachments and selected Canvas/Element references. Reuse an authorized single-person identity that the user has chosen; never select the latest node, a filename, or a person from a group photo by inference. The identity gate is the visual anchor only; it does not approve the keyframe previs, voice, character subject, or video.

For a local revision, reuse the identity recorded in the existing project. A text or overlay-only edit that creates no new presenter media does not reopen this gate.

If no person is supplied, read Presenter identity [blocked]: one ordinary show_form, exact account-available Midjourney v8.2, a 2:3 headshot on #808080, a short English prompt ending in --style raw, exact-result inspection, then explicit user adoption. Do not require a provider output count or reject a supported Midjourney result because of its returned shape. Use the route's live structured parameters for ratio, resolution, and quality. Do not use a beauty fallback or nearby-version fallback.

Keep the selected business route while waiting. Before identity adoption, do not generate presenter media. Already supplied facts and copy remain inputs; never discard or recollect them. Once adopted, the same exact face reference serves every route.

Required production sequence

For a new presenter-led video, keep this order. Skip a stage only when its approved artifact already exists and is still valid for the requested change.

Lock the brief and aspect. Collect audience, objective, script or topic, duration, and orientation. Use landscape 16:9 or portrait 9:16 according to the brief; if it is genuinely ambiguous, ask before generating. Resolve the live model contract for the exact ratio instead of guessing a provider parameter.

Create the visual identity. Reuse an explicitly approved person or follow Presenter identity [blocked] to use Midjourney v8.2 for the raw headshot. The prompt must describe one person and one casting headshot; do not turn it into multiple casting options or enumerate candidate identities. Inspect the result(s) returned by the live route and wait for explicit adoption of one face anchor; keep that anchor fixed afterward.

Select and fix the voice. Reuse an approved voice. For a user-designated upload, inspect its exact audio reference and bind it as voice_ref; an explicit request to use that voice counts as selection. Do not generate alternative voices for it. Otherwise resolve the newest available Seed Audio model, generate a small voice candidate set (default two) using the same short audition line, let the user listen and choose, and bind that result as voice_ref. Use fast, clear speech and lively intonation. Read the live model contract before generating; do not hard-code an assumed latest version. Keep this voice identity for every subsequent audio job.

Build and confirm the keyframe scene. After the face and voice are approved, use the live GPT 2.5 model contract to make the minimum keyframe previs for the requested scene(s), with the selected person, scene, action, framing, and locked 16:9 or 9:16 ratio. Pass the adopted face as the identity reference; describe a real human in a live-action scene. For product and property, include the subject in the keyframe plan: presenter framing, presenter_with_object or presenter_in_space when the relation matters, product/space hero, close-up or detail, and the return to the presenter. Generate one keyframe per distinct composition. For course, cover the presenter, concept_visual, worked_example, and any screen_demo or html_recording frame required by the learning beat. For news, cover the news_anchor, headline/source card, timeline, chart/map/quote frame, and return to the anchor needed by the source claims. A continuous shot can reuse its approved keyframe across several audio segments. Use a few concise sentences for person, action, framing, setting, object/space detail, and light. Put aspect, count, and quality in supported structured parameters. Inspect the exact person-in-scene and subject keyframes and get explicit approval.

Create the character subject. Only after the keyframe scene is approved, create or update the character subject/Element through the current persistence contract. Bind the adopted face, selected voice_ref, approved scene/keyframe references, and only the requested Look assets. Preserve unrelated members.

Generate the first talking scene. Prepare the first scene's spoken audio with the selected Seed Audio voice anchor with fast delivery and lively, varied intonation, then use Seedance 2.5 for the first talking-video segment and the continuation workflow. Seedance 2.0 or MiniMax H3 remain alternatives for separate video requests when selected by the user; never silently switch an explicitly chosen model. The video prompt must require a real human presenter, fast but clear speech, varied expressions that follow the meaning, natural eye contact, head movements, and gestures. Bind the character subject, approved keyframe, scene-one audio, exact spoken copy, locked aspect, and timing. For product and property, generate presenter and cutaway source clips as separate shot units, then assemble their approved order on the timeline. For course, generate presenter A-roll and each teaching B-roll unit separately; record approved HTML/CSS/JS visuals before assembly and export the assembled lesson timeline to Canvas through the supported path. Inspect the exact completed first scene and its first teaching or subject cutaway before continuing. For news, search and verify the source ledger before writing the final lines, then generate the presenter A-roll and source-labelled HTML B-roll separately. Any HTML-to-video recording must use the installed ffmpeg and headless Chromium chain before the assembled bulletin is exported to Canvas.

 

Reuse this compact performance clause in each video prompt, then add only the scene-specific action and continuity details:

Make the next scene audio and extend. After the first scene is accepted, generate the next scene's audio with the same voice_ref and the current Seed Audio contract. Extend the continuous presenter A-roll in Seedance 2.5 using the immediately preceding accepted presenter video, the new scene audio, the same subject, and supported scene/keyframe context. For product and property, put approved B-roll over the A-roll in the final timeline. For course, place each approved teaching visual under the matching voice_span; HTML recordings and source captures remain independent B-roll unless the live contract explicitly supports their continuation. Only use a direct A→B or B→A video continuation when the live contract explicitly supports that shot-type change; otherwise generate the B-roll independently and keep its voiceover span in the renderer manifest. Scene 2 uses scene 1's accepted predecessor, scene 3 uses scene 2's accepted predecessor, and so on. Keep voice, aspect, and performance consistent. Follow the runtime contract for continuity, output overlap, and audio timing; stop when the complete approved script has been spoken and the requested deliverable is covered. For news, keep the source-labelled HTML B-roll independent unless the live contract explicitly supports a shot-type change, and assemble it under the matching verified news voice_span.

Product and property cutaway layer

Read the selected Product method [blocked] or Property method [blocked] for the route-specific shot grammar. The shared rule is:

Keep presenter speech, product/space visuals, and sourced proof as separate shot units. A cutaway may carry the continuing approved voiceover, but it must not be hidden inside a talking-head generation prompt.
Give every shot a shot_type, source_ref, script_span, voice_span, duration, transition point, and acceptance state. Use presenter for A-roll, presenter_with_object or presenter_in_space for a person-subject relationship, object_hero or object_detail for product views, demo_action for use, and space_wide, space_detail, or amenity for property views.
Alternate on purpose: presenter establishes the claim, the product or space proves it visually, and the presenter returns for interpretation or CTA. Do not cut on every sentence or use an insert that has no spoken or evidentiary role.
Generate object/space clips separately from presenter clips. For a real product, UI, address, room, amenity, measurement, label, or price, use supplied or captured source media whenever exact appearance matters. Generated subject footage is illustrative until matched to an approved source. Keep pure B-roll prompts short: object/space, shot size, action, light, and continuity detail. Use the real-human, fast, expressive performance clause only for presenter or presenter_with_object shots, never for a product/space-only closeup.
Assemble only after the individual clips and their audio spans are approved. Check that cuts preserve the fixed person, product identity, spatial orientation, speech continuity, safe areas, and readable labels. An ordered clip list is partial when a rendered master was requested.
Course teaching B-roll layer

Read the selected Course method [blocked] for the full teaching contract. The shared rule is:

Keep on-camera presenter A-roll and teaching B-roll as separate shot units. Use presenter for goals, explanations, judgment, correction, recap, and practice; use presenter_with_visual when the relationship between the person and visual is itself instructional.
Use concept_visual for an illustrative GPT visual, html_recording for exact UI/code/formula/chart/table/timeline states, screen_demo for supplied or captured procedures, worked_example for sourced calculations, and caption_card for exact definitions or warnings. Do not use generated imagery as an exact UI, live-data, official-chart, or completed-experiment substitute.
Give every teaching unit a learning_step or claim_id, visual_mode, source_ref or html_artifact_ref, script_span, voice_span, duration, cut-in/cut-out, evidence_role, and review_state. For HTML, also record the artifact version, viewport, frame rate, duration, start/end state, and recording reference before export.
Keep approved voiceover under silent B-roll only within its matching voice_span; return to on-camera presenter delivery for interpretation, correction, emphasis, recap, or the next action. Cut on a teaching event such as a visual reveal, code action, formula change, or worked result instead of cutting only for variety.
Export the assembled course timeline to Canvas through the supported renderer or write-back path and read back the returned Canvas reference. An HTML preview, local recording, A-roll clip set, or unordered B-roll list is partial when a lesson video was requested.
News bulletin layer

Read the selected News method [blocked] before planning a news video. News is a source-verification and visual-evidence route, not a generic market or talking-head route:

Search the network before writing the final script or generating news visuals. Fix the source cutoff time, timezone, geography, language, audience, and freshness window. Prefer primary sources, then independently corroborate material claims. Keep facts, source claims, interpretation, and unresolved items separate.
Give every claim a source URL/document, title, publication or update time, search and access time, source type, status, exact source span, and claim_id. A 403, login wall, missing date, or stale page is an access/freshness gap, not proof that no update exists.
Use a deliberate A/B sequence: news_anchor says what happened, source-labelled HTML B-roll shows the headline, timeline, chart, map, quote, or source strip, and the anchor returns to explain impact, uncertainty, or the next item. Keep each B-roll unit tied to one verified claim_id and voice_span.
Any HTML-to-video or page-recording path is fixed to the installed stack: ffmpeg and headless Chromium are installed. Headless Chromium renders the deterministic page at the locked viewport; ffmpeg encodes or packages the captured frames and audio into video. A browser preview, HTML file, or search-result screenshot is not a finished video. Record browser/ffmpeg versions, viewport, fps, duration, start/end state, output reference, source cutoff, and Canvas reference.
Export the assembled bulletin to Canvas and read back the returned reference. If network search, source ledger, fixed-stack recording, or Canvas write-back is unavailable, report the news result as partial and preserve the exact gap.

Do not add a separate image or exploratory keyframe generation stage solely to create selection candidates, and do not force a provider-specific image count. Keep the Midjourney prompt focused on one person; use the result shape returned by the live route and bind only the image the user explicitly adopts as the face anchor. Voice candidates remain the intentional selection set. If a visual, voice, or video result is rejected, regenerate only that stage after the user supplies a changed direction; keep approved stages and references unchanged.

Use "real human" and positive performance direction in generation prompts. Do not label the subject “digital human”, “AI avatar”, or “virtual presenter”, even in a stock negative clause. Avoid stiff posture, frozen expressions, mechanical nodding, or looping gestures in the result. This describes the desired visual performance; retain truthful synthetic-media context in delivery.

Shared execution
Establish the brief. Read the selected route's method, reuse known inputs, and collect only blocking gaps: audience, objective, exact facts/source media, script or prompt, orientation, duration, voice, and final deliverables.
Plan the staged artifacts. Preserve supplied exact copy. For a topic prompt, produce the full spoken script, compact GPT 2.5 presenter/subject keyframe prompts, shot plan, cutaway and teaching-visual source list, per-claim source ledger, and per-scene audio lines before generation. For course, choose a visual mode for every beat (gpt_visual, html_recording, source_capture, or uploaded_broll) before generation. For news, complete network search and the source ledger before final script, HTML, or A-roll generation. Reuse existing approval for unchanged work. Asset-only requests follow asset.md and do not enter video production.
Record dependencies. Track route, aspect, identity reference/state, keyframe references, approved script, voice candidates and selected voice_ref, character subject, facts/sources, scene ids, shot types, cutaway source refs, spoken lines/audio results, media/reference roles, overlay/caption text, teaching learning_step/claim_id, visual mode, HTML artifact and recording references, news source URL/title/published-at/accessed-at/status/cutoff fields, browser and ffmpeg versions, viewport, fps, timing, cut order, segment chain, exact job/result references, Canvas export and read-back references, review state, and export state. This is a project manifest, not a new Element schema or backend API.
Execute the current contract. Read Runtime contract [blocked] before generation, media inspection, persistence, or rendering. Use standard TapNow CLI and existing forms. For every HTML-to-video/page-recording task, verify the installed stack exactly as ffmpeg and headless Chromium are installed before capture; do not substitute a browser preview or an untracked recorder. A source reference, submitted job, completed media result, inspected result, and final export are distinct states.
Review the smallest changed unit. Keep the face anchor, keyframes, voice, and accepted assets fixed. Re-render changed information cards without regenerating the presenter; regenerate a spoken line only when speech changed. Changing a scene's audio regenerates that scene's video. A changed video invalidates downstream continuations that used it as their source; preserve earlier scenes and recheck or regenerate affected continuations. A new identity invalidates dependent presenter visuals; a new voice invalidates dependent speech and talking video. For product or property work, a changed object/space source invalidates only the affected cutaway and any downstream assembly that depends on its timing. For course, a changed claim, formula, code result, HTML artifact, source capture, or learning step invalidates its teaching shot, narration/caption timing, and dependent assembly, while preserving unrelated chapters. For news, a changed source, cutoff, claim, date, number, quote, or HTML evidence card invalidates that claim's source ledger row, A-roll line, B-roll recording, captions, and dependent assembly.
Deliver the real result. Match the requested asset or video scope. A full business video requires an actual assembled export; an A-roll clip or ordered segment set is partial when assembly was requested. Report missing runtime capabilities and remaining work precisely. Do not publish externally.
Interaction and acceptance
Keep form submission, identity adoption, voice confirmation, keyframe-previs approval, subject creation, platform cost confirmation, and final review separate. Honor authorization already given for the same scope; do not stack duplicate forms or add confirmation at every scene.
Preserve the presenter's truthful role. Generated presenters do not create evidence of customer experience, credentials, real locations, product performance, or financial outcomes. Apply the selected route's specific evidence rules.
Inspect exact completed media for identity continuity, fixed voice, complete speech, lip sync, fast clear delivery, expressive natural movement, facts, caption/chart legibility, teaching order, HTML/screen readability, timing, cut order, cutaway continuity, product/space identity, news source ledger and cutoff, publication/ access times, fixed ffmpeg + headless Chromium recording state, Canvas export state, safe areas, and the CTA or next learning action. Frozen faces, stiff movement, repeated gestures, voice drift, unexplained cuts, or skipped/repeated lines fail review. State which checks could not run; structural validation alone is not visual acceptance.
Deliver exact asset/media references, the script or captions when relevant, sources/rights and synthetic-presenter context, unresolved items, and the actual export status. Do not promise virality, sales, or guaranteed outcomes.
